corrected_value.title: Young children’s intuitive understanding of rectangular area measurement

decision.location: Abstract (line 5), Publisher highlight (line 8), and Crossref deposited reference metadata (line 12)
decision.quote: Since Battista et al.’s (1998) and Outhred and Mitchelmore’s (2000) studies over 20 years ago, spatial structuring of rectangular arrays have been examined with a wide variety of tasks and protocols. Despite observations that tasks can affect such reasoning, there has been little specific focus on examining how task and protocol structure affect students’ spatial structuring. This paper presents a constructive replication study with third-grade students and the inclusion of eye-gaze data from mobile eye-tracking headsets. Findings confirm previously identified levels, while identifying task features that coincide with higher levels of spatial structuring.
decision.reason: The abstract and publisher highlight ('A constructive replication study of Battista et al. (1998) and Outhred and Mitchelmore (2000) was conducted.') explicitly establish that the paper empirically re-tests both Battista et al. (1998) and Outhred and Mitchelmore (2000) in a new sample of third-grade students and compares its findings against the levels previously identified in those studies. The article's deposited Crossref reference metadata (line 12, key 10.1016/j.jmathb.2026.101352_bib31) identifies the second target as Outhred (in-text: Outhred and Mitchelmore, 2000), 'Young children’s intuitive understanding of rectangular area measurement', Journal for Research in Mathematics Education 31(2): 144, DOI 10.2307/749749. The only shipped row (input_row_index 1293, DOI 10.5951/jresematheduc.29.5.0503) represents the sibling target Battista et al. (1998), 'Students' Spatial Structuring of 2D Arrays of Squares', Journal for Research in Mathematics Education 29(5): 503-532 (key bib5, DOI 10.2307/749731). Outhred and Mitchelmore (2000) is an independent study by different authors published two years later, so report equivalence does not apply and this original work is genuinely absent from the shipped rows. decision.quote: In our extension, we failed to find support for the findings by Kogut and Ritov (2007) that there is a higher likelihood of helping single victims over a group if they belong to the ingroup (vs. the outgroup).
